title: Comparison refuses to insert or delete a paragraph holding a simple field
symptom: compare refuses with "cannot track a whole paragraph's simple field outside a field it replaces", so a heading added under a table of contents made by insert_toc cannot be compared
workaround: add or remove the paragraph by hand on the redline

title: Comparison refuses a paragraph moved after a final table, or added or deleted after a moved or redlined final table
symptom: compare refuses with "needs an adjacent paragraph for a final paragraph move" or "... for a final paragraph change" (after a table moved to the end), or "holds an existing tracked revision" (after a table that holds tracked changes)
workaround: put a paragraph after the table in both versions, or resolve the earlier tracked changes on both copies first

title: Text replacement through Python is slower than the CLI
symptom: about 1.5 times the time of the CLI for the same pairs
workaround: when only replacing, use `oxoffice docx replace FILE --map pairs.json`

title: Edits cost more as the document grows, most on files saved by Word or Google Docs
symptom: Run.text, Paragraph.text, add_run, Table.add_row, remove_content and notes cost the whole body: tens of milliseconds per call, up to seconds on long reports
workaround: batch the edits, or build the content aside and insert it once

title: Form operations cost seconds on long documents
symptom: about 0.1 s at 25 paragraphs, 3 to 9 s at 1,000
workaround: pass every rule in one call

title: Non-breaking hyphens and positional tabs are missing from paragraph text
symptom: Paragraph text and text search skip w:noBreakHyphen and w:ptab, so "co-op" written with a non-breaking hyphen reads "coop", a search for "co-op" finds nothing, and replacing "coop" leaves the hyphen after the replacement
workaround: search for the text on each side of the hyphen or positional tab

title: Word files saved in another language: new comments do not use the file's comment styles
symptom: a comment added to a Word file with localised style ids, such as Commentaire, gets new CommentText and CommentReference styles based on Normal, so it does not look like Word's comments
workaround: set the new comment's paragraphs and its reference mark to the file's comment styles, the styles named "annotation text" and "annotation reference"

title: Removing a paragraph leaves its notes behind
symptom: remove_content keeps the paragraph's footnotes and endnotes as unreferenced notes
workaround: remove the paragraph's notes first (remove_footnote, remove_endnote, same names in Python)

title: A list item numbered through its style cannot be restarted
symptom: restart_numbering fails with "paragraph has no explicit numbering level" on the List Number paragraphs of Word and python-docx files, whose numbering comes from the style
workaround: Rust: give the paragraph its own numbering first (set_numbering with the num_id and level of effective_paragraph_properties), then restart; Python: start a new list (add_numbering_definition, add_numbering_instance, Paragraph.numbering)

title: Content control values keep the prompt's style, and text() glues a block control's paragraphs
symptom: a value set on a control showing its prompt stays greyed out in Word, a line feed shows as a space, extra paragraphs stay empty, a combo box refuses free text, and text() runs paragraphs together
workaround: read a block control's paragraphs one by one with story_paragraphs: they are the entries whose location path is [i, 0], [i, 1]..., i being the control's index in story_items (index_path in Python)

title: The tag setters do not reach content controls in headers
symptom: set_content_control_value_by_tag returns 0 for a control in a header and content_controls() lists body controls only; `oxoffice docx fill` fails with "no content control has tag" (--tag) or "requires exactly one target" (--values)
workaround: fill_form with a rule naming the tag (a content control tag target), which reaches every story (same name in Python); none through the CLI

title: A date content control in Word's long date format cannot be set
symptom: setting a control formatted d MMMM yyyy fails with "unsupported or missing date format", and protect_form refuses rules naming it
workaround: give the control a yyyy-MM-dd or dd/MM/yyyy date format first (set_content_control_type, same name in Python), then set the value; none through the CLI

title: PDF pages: a blank page before a section break, endnotes over a final table, outline entries on the wrong page
symptom: a page break just before a next-page section break leaves a blank page; endnotes overlap a table that ends the document; an outline entry opens the page before a heading moved by keep with next
workaround: remove the page break before a next-page section break; end the document with a paragraph after a final table; put a page break before such a heading

title: PDF text: right-to-left paragraphs start at the left margin, CJK text is drawn as boxes by default
symptom: a right-to-left paragraph is drawn against the left margin, and Chinese, Japanese and Korean glyphs are empty boxes with the default render options
workaround: none for right-to-left paragraphs (an explicit right alignment would move them left in Word and LibreOffice); for CJK, pass a CJK font file (Rust to_pdf_with_fonts, or to_pdfa_with_fonts_deterministic for PDF/A; Python to_pdf(fonts=...) or font_dir=...; CLI convert --font-dir) or turn system fonts on (Rust to_pdf_with_options with use_system_fonts, Python to_pdf(system_fonts=True), CLI convert --system-fonts); none for PDF/A in Python and the CLI

title: PDF endnotes are numbered 1, 2, 3 instead of i, ii, iii
symptom: endnotes without a number format of their own are numbered in decimal in the PDF, where Word numbers them in lower roman
workaround: set the endnote policy's number format to lower roman (set_note_policy, same name in Python) before converting; none through the CLI

title: Comparison refuses an endnote added, removed or moved, or a change it writes as a deletion and an insertion around an endnote
symptom: compare refuses with "endnotes story shell count changed", "identical related-story shells" or "its reference moved to another site" (also when a table or paragraph holding an endnote is replaced whole), and with endnotes ignored "ignored endnotes cannot supply the edited reference to endnote N" when the edited version references an endnote the original does not hold
workaround: make the endnote change on the accepted result after comparing, or compare that pair in Word

title: Word and character counts and the heading list leave out text inserted with tracked changes
symptom: word_count and character_count (Rust, Python, CLI info) and headings / document_outline (Rust) read a paragraph's direct runs, so a document edited with tracking on counts fewer words than text() holds
workaround: count the words of the accepted paragraph texts, and their characters paragraph by paragraph (text() adds a line feed after each paragraph and a tab between cells): Rust text(), Python the .text of doc.paragraphs and of table cell paragraphs, CLI paragraphs[].text of oxoffice docx text --json; read headings from numbered_document_outline (Rust)

title: A floating picture added by add_anchored_image gets the alt text "Background"
symptom: Rust add_anchored_image writes descr="Background" on every picture it adds, which Word shows and screen readers read aloud
workaround: Rust: add the picture with add_picture_with_options, anchor set and the description wanted; Python add_picture and the CLI do not take this path

title: A presentation part with a control character is refused at open
symptom: open fails with "PackageError ... holds U+0001" and `oxoffice pptx validate` exits 1, while PowerPoint opens the file
workaround: remove the character from that part's bytes, then open the file

title: Importing slides with their source formatting refuses PowerPoint and Google slides that have notes
symptom: import_slides with keep_source_formatting fails with "unrepresentable source notes-master ... authority", calling the producer's part malformed
workaround: import onto this deck's layouts instead, without keeping the source formatting

title: Sections do not follow added, duplicated, imported or moved slides
symptom: a new slide belongs to no section, and a moved slide stays listed in its old section
workaround: set the sections again after the slide edits (set_sections in Rust and Python); none through the CLI

title: Google tables cannot lose columns down to one
symptom: remove_column fails with "table frame size must remain positive"
workaround: before removing columns, set the first column to its own width (Rust set_column_width, Python column.width) to resync the frame
